Subject: Nucleus AI trial — traffic profile & POC timeline (recap + action items)

Thanks again for the call earlier — good discussion. Wanted to capture the post-call recap and concrete next steps so we can lock the POC plan quickly. Short version up top, details and asks below.

Recap (quick):
- Goal: 2-week trial to validate inference latency, cost per request, and end-to-end behavior with your summarization and reranking pipelines.
- Success criteria (customer-proposed + my suggestions):
  * avg latency (p95) <= 350ms for summary endpoint at target concurrency
  * token-level cost <= target threshold (we'll populate after we size the workload)
  * no quality regressions on 12 canonical prompts (we'll exchange prompt set)
- Tentative window: July 6 — July 20 (flexible)

Immediate asks (can you provide by EOD Tue 6/30):
1) Fill the attached CSV (nucleus_poc_workload_table.csv) with representative workload numbers for these buckets: steady-state RPS, expected peak RPS and duration, typical and max token lengths, concurrency, and common request patterns (e.g., many short requests vs fewer long ones).
2) Confirm which endpoints you want in the POC: summary, rerank, embeddings (if you want embeddings included we need a small sample).
3) Share the 12 canonical prompts for quality checks (we'll treat these as eval seeds).
4) Confirm primary POC contact and procurement timeline (we'll need a signed form if you require an MSA/PO).

Suggested next steps & owners:
- Nucleus: populate workload CSV, share prompts, confirm contacts (Lisa/Tom) — owner: Lisa
- Redwood: create POC environment, snapshot config, provide cost/throughput estimates — owner: Lauren
- Ops validation and capacity planning — owner: Marcus

Notes on how we typically size POCs (so you know what we need in CSV):
- RPS buckets (steady / peak / burst duration)
- Average tokens per request and 95th percentile
- Concurrency during peak and expected cache reuse patterns
- Any sequence-length heavy jobs (e.g., doc summarization where request length > 2k tokens)

Attachments: nucleus_poc_workload_table.csv (CSV: workload buckets — please return with numbers), redwood_poc_template.md (POC template we will use)

If anything above looks off, flag it and we'll adjust. Otherwise I'll start drafting the internal config once I get your filled CSV.

Thanks — talk soon.

On Sun, Jun 28, 2026 at 3:02 PM Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Recap (quick):
> - Goal: 2-week trial...

Prelim workload notes (please treat as estimates; we'll confirm by EOD Tue):
- Steady-state RPS: 3 RPS (background job + user-initiated summaries).
- Typical peak: 60 RPS for short bursts (2–3 minutes) during morning syncs and campaign pushes.
- Sustained peak (multi-hour): 12–15 RPS for longer runs when we batch-run nightly summaries.
- Typical tokens per request: ~850 tokens (mostly source docs + instruction).
- 95th percentile tokens: ~2200 tokens (long reports). We rarely exceed ~4000 tokens but we do have occasional edge cases.
- Concurrency: normal concurrency 6–8, but during 60-RPS bursts concurrency hits ~40 due to many short requests in parallel.
- Burst pattern: short high-frequency spikes (1–3 min) ~3x/week; predictable nightly batches 22:00–01:00 local where throughput is steadier.

Endpoints for POC:
- Summary endpoint (primary)
- Rerank (secondary) — we'll include a small sample set
- No embeddings in phase 1

POC window: July 6 — July 20 works for us. Procurement: procurement@nucl.ai is the contact for PO/MSA; they expect a 7–10 day turnaround after we get the final SOW.

Thanks for the forward — reviewed Lisa's CSV. High-level recommendations and ballpark numbers below (will refine if workload numbers change):

Recommended config (POC):
- Model family: rw-instruct-7b (default) or rw-instruct-13b-quant (if Nucleus wants lower latency at slightly higher cost).
- Quantization: q4f16 for 13b if memory is a constraint; q8_0 for 7b if you want best perf/cost.
- Batching: enable dynamic batching up to 64 tokens/request to cover common short requests; keep max batch size tuned to maintain p95 <= 350ms.
- Caching: enable prefix KV caching for repetitive summary prompts — expect ~10–20% token cost reduction for high reuse patterns.

Throughput & latency estimates (approx):
- For rw-instruct-7b (q8): steady 3 RPS -> trivial. Under 60-RPS 2–3 min bursts, a single 80GB GPU with autoscaling to 2 GPUs for bursts should handle peaks with p95 ~ 250–320ms (depends on exact token lengths).
- For rw-instruct-13b-quant (q4f16): p95 ~ 300–350ms at higher cost; need 2 GPUs baseline for concurrency headroom and autoscale to 3 for short 60-RPS bursts.

Cost note (very rough, pro-rated for 2-week window):
- 7b (hosted): estimated GPU-hours 200 -> pro-rated cost estimate (incl infra + tokens) ~ $6k–$9k for 2 weeks.
- 13b-quant: GPU-hours 320 -> estimate ~ $10k–$15k.
(We'll refine after Marcus validates instance sizing and exact GPU types.)

Ops considerations:
- Cold starts: first hour of the POC may show higher p95 while caches warm. Recommend a warm-up script (we can supply) to run before the customer starts evaluation windows.
- Long sequences: for requests >2k tokens, expect throughput drop; if Nucleus has many of these, we should flag for a different batching strategy or increase GPU memory.

I can pull more precise token/sec numbers and simulated p95 latencies if Marcus confirms the exact instance classes we plan to use. If the team is aligned I'll prepare a short technical appendix to attach to the SOW.
